primitives.name: Survivorship Bias Correction
primitives.verbatim_quote: In particular, the aging effects are not often determined from a full population of athletes in a given league.
primitives.assumptions: Players who leave the league early are systematically different from those who stay; the missing data mechanism depends on unobserved performance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Early retirement due to poor performance creates a right-censoring bias in observed aging curves.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian survival analysis with informative dropout priors, conformal predictive intervals for counterfactual trajectories.
layer2.telemetry: Observed vs. imputed career length distributions, proportion of early retirees by age bin.

primitives.name: Multiple Imputation Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: We first perform a simulation study to evaluate the effects of different dropout mechanisms on the estimation of aging curves.
primitives.assumptions: Missing data are MAR conditional on prior performance and age; the imputation model captures true underlying performance dynamics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High-dimensional missingness patterns lead to unstable point estimates without proper uncertainty quantification.

layer2.mapping: Multilevel mixed-effects models with Gibbs sampling for posterior draws, Rubin's combination rules for pooled inference.
layer2.telemetry: Imputation MSE, percentage of converged chains, effective sample size per imputed value.

primitives.name: Aging Curve Estimation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The average performance of players by age throughout their careers is visually represented by an aging curve.
primitives.assumptions: Performance metrics are measured with error; career trajectories follow smooth latent functions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overestimation occurs when ignoring the truncation induced by player removal from the league.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian nonparametric regression (e.g., Gaussian processes) with dropout-adjusted likelihoods, conformal prediction for robust bandits.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared prediction error on held-out careers, coverage rates of credible bands, peak age estimates.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core issue is that observed career trajectories are censored by survival decisions, leading to biased slope estimates in standard OLS. Multiple imputation addresses this by generating plausible completions under a MAR assumption, while accounting for the heteroskedasticity introduced by dropout. However, if the imputation model fails to capture the dependence between performance and termination risk, the resulting curves will still suffer from omitted variable bias. A key diagnostic is comparing the distribution of imputed versus observed outcomes in early careers, where dropout is minimal.
